children.name: Special Education and Accessibility
children.blurb: A review of research on AI with students with disabilities found something uncomfortable. Much of the work described AI as a way to relieve adults of the burden of working with these students, rather than as a way to empower the students and their families (Rice, 2023).

children.name: English Learners and Newcomers
children.blurb: In a trial with 217 second graders learning English, most of them Latino, a computer tutor taught the vocabulary of science and social studies units. Students who used it learned more of the taught words than students who did not, with an effect of 0.38 (Baker et al., 2020).

children.name: Communicating With Families
children.blurb: A school district once had a problem with truancy notices. The letters sent to families were written in legal language, warning of consequences and citing the education code.

children.name: Wellbeing, Behavior, Attendance, and Safety
children.blurb: A study of 14 companies that monitor students online found that most watch students around the clock, not just during school hours. Most use AI to flag concerning content, but fewer than half described any human review of those flags.

children.name: Counseling, College, and Career
children.blurb: Every spring, many high school graduates are admitted to college, plan to go, and never show up in the fall. Researchers call this summer melt.

sections.body: This part of school life covers the students and families who need the most careful attention, including special education and accessibility, English learners and newcomers, communication with families, wellbeing and safety, and counseling and college. AI in these areas is described as a support to the people closest to the student, not a replacement for them. The book treats these chapters as holding some of the strongest evidence in the Volume, with several randomized trials involving messages to families and support for students after high school. The work here is about reaching every student and every family, not only those easiest to serve.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: What works, according to the book, includes messages to families and support for students after high school, which appear in several of the strongest randomized trials in the Volume. What does not work is letting AI take over decisions that must stay with people, and the book holds firm rules about this. The rule it holds to is that these decisions remain human, even where the evidence for AI support is strong. Careful attention to the students and families who most need it is the standard the book applies throughout.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages fit together as the practical chapters of this Part. A teacher would go to Special Education and Accessibility and to English Learners and Newcomers for the students who need the most careful attention in the classroom. A leader would go to Communicating With Families and to Wellbeing, Behavior, Attendance, and Safety for the systems that connect school to home and keep students safe. A parent or counselor would go to Counseling, College, and Career for the path after high school, where the book notes some of its strongest evidence and its firmest rules about decisions that must stay with people.
